ThirtyTwo is primarily known for snowboard boots; this is their first snowboard product [17] 137. ThirtyTwo boots brand reputation: Strong, well-established — "rider-driven since 1995" [14] 138. ThirtyTwo boot reputation on forums: Generally positive for comfort after break-in; some sizing inconsistency noted [40][41] 139. Nidecker Group is considered the second biggest snowboard company in the world [10] 140. ThirtyTwo's snowboard line uses SWS factory, same factory that manufactures boards for Jones, YES, Nidecker, Rome, Bataleon, and other brands [6][16][42] 141. Brand director Brian Cook confirmed boards are built to Scott's specifications [5] 142. Board development approach: Custom shapes, moulds, and a real point of difference — "We didn't want to slap graphics on existing boards" [18] 143. First-year brand entering a competitive market — lack of long-term durability and performance track record is a relevant risk consideration 144. Scott Stevens has been on the ThirtyTwo team for more than 17 years (boots/outerwear) [5] 145. Scott Stevens is best known for his skate-style riding [6] 146. Stevens' riding style: Creativity and ability to transform overlooked features into expressive technical lines [21] 147. Stevens has shaped the evolution of jibbing for more than two decades [21] 148. ThirtyTwo snowboard team riders (as of early 2026): Pat Fava, Phil Hansen, Patrick Hofmann, Brin Alexander, Scott Stevens, Ellie Weiler [6][16] 149. Burton Custom Camber: Directional twin, camber, Flex 6/10, $679.95 — more all-mountain oriented, stiffer [29] 154. Endeavor Pioneer: True twin, camber, Flex 5, $599 — similar spec and price point [30] 155. YES Greats: All-mountain freestyle twin, hybrid camber, highly rated in category reviews [44] 156. Jones Tweaker: True twin, playful and creative, soft flex — more playful/softer than Middle Earth [44] 157. Rome Agent Pro: All-mountain freestyle twin, consistent performer across terrain [44] 158. Burton Blossom: True twin, traditional camber, mid flex, freestyle focused — similar concept but from an established board maker [28] 159. Lib Tech Off Ramp: Twin all-mountain freestyle with camber, good edge hold — strong competitor on ice [28] 160. Key differentiator from competitors: Limited edition collectibility + Scott Stevens pro model + ThirtyTwo's brand-new entry into snowboards makes this a unique market proposition 161. Collectible appeal: "A board that'll live past its days on snow as wall-hanging art" — general sentiment about thirtytwo board graphics [17]
